cisco_ios_xe_logging.description: Comprehensive reference for Cisco IOS XE system message logging (syslog), including format, severity levels, facilities, destinations, commands, and advanced features. Applies to Catalyst switches, ASR/ISR routers, and IOS XE Catalyst SD-WAN devices.

examples: *Mar  1 18:46:11.483 UTC: %LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface GigabitEthernet0/1, changed state to up
00:00:46: %LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface Port-channel1, changed state to up

components.name: timestamp
components.description: Optional date/time or uptime (controlled by 'service timestamps log ...')

components.name: FACILITY
components.description: 2+ uppercase letters identifying the source (hardware device, protocol, or software module)

components.name: MNEMONIC
components.description: Unique short code that identifies the specific message

components.name: description / Message-text
components.description: Human-readable details; may contain variable fields such as interface names, IP addresses, etc.

severity_notes: Specifying a severity level logs that level and all numerically lower (more severe) levels.
Default console severity is usually debugging (7).
Default remote trap severity is often informational (6).

common_facilities.description: IOS XE Catalyst SD-WAN specific facilities (FTMD, OMP, VDAEMON, CFGMGR, etc.)

logging_destinations.notes: Requires terminal monitor on the session
UDP default; TCP/TLS for reliable/secure delivery
Used with snmp-server enable traps syslog

key_configuration_commands.description: Add date/time timestamps to log messages
Add uptime timestamps to log messages
Add sequence numbers to log messages
Set the syslog facility code sent to remote servers (default local7; range local0–local7)
Set the source IP interface for remote syslog packets
Limit severity of messages sent to remote syslog hosts
Use RFC 5424 format for remote syslog (supported on newer releases)
Create a message discriminator for filtering
Synchronize logging with command output on a line

advanced_features.description: Tcl-based framework for filtering, correlating, escalating, routing, and customizing system logging messages before delivery
Filter messages by facility, mnemonic, message body (regex), severity, and rate-limit. Checked in order: severity → facility → mnemonic → body → rate-limit
Optional structured XML output for messages
TCP, BEEP, and TLS (RFC 5425) transports in addition to default UDP
Deeper daemon-level tracing available on some platforms and IOS XE SD-WAN devices

default_behavior.timestamps: Often disabled by default (recommended to enable)

relation_to_sdwan.note: On IOS XE Catalyst SD-WAN devices, both standard IOS XE messages (%LINK-..., %LINEPROTO-..., %SYS-..., etc.) and SD-WAN-specific messages (facilities such as FTMD, OMP, VDAEMON, CFGMGR, or prefixes like %Cisco-SDWAN-... / %SDWAN-...) are generated.

notes: There are thousands of individual messages; the authoritative list is the System Message Guide for the specific IOS XE release.
Variable fields in message text are often shown in documentation as [chars], [dec], [hex], [inet], etc.
Some messages include traceback information for debugging.
Exact available facilities, commands, and defaults vary by platform and IOS XE release (16.x, 17.x, 26.x, etc.).
primary_sources: Cisco IOS XE System Message Guide (per-release, e.g. 17.14.x, 17.16.x, 17.18.x, 26.x)
System Management Configuration Guide – Configuring System Message Logs
Cisco IOS XE Command Reference – Logging Commands
Cisco IOS XE Catalyst SD-WAN Qualified Command Reference (for SD-WAN specific logging options)
